meta.title: Who really said "Football is not a matter of life and death. It's much more important than that"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Shankly’s idea, not his sentence. The documented line comes from a Granada TV interview on 20 May 1981 — and it is worded differently.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Football is not a matter of life and death. It's much more important than that'?
meta.ogDescription: What Bill Shankly actually said on camera in May 1981 — and why the famous version is a later paraphrase.

answer.label: Bill Shankly — but not in these words
answer.sourceLine: The thought is his and it was said on camera, but not as the polished epigram people share. In a Granada Television interview with Shelley Rohde broadcast on 20 May 1981, Shankly said: “Somebody said that football’s a matter of life and death to you. I said, ‘Listen, it’s more important than that.’” — he was quoting someone else’s remark back at them, and he said it moments after admitting he regretted what football had cost his family. Wikipedia notes the quotation is frequently paraphrased ↗, and the familiar one-liner is one of those paraphrases.

source.excerpt: Yeah, I regret it very much… Somebody said that football’s a matter of life and death to you. I said, ‘Listen, it’s more important than that.’
trail: The sentence people share — “Football is not a matter of life and death. It’s much more important than that” — circulates without a source. Goodreads carries exactly that wording ↗ under its own standing disclaimer that community-added quotes are not verified.

A longer variant runs in the press too: the Daily Mirror’s football blog printed “Some people believe football is a matter of life and death, I am very disappointed with that attitude. I can assure you it is much, much more important than that” in a Shankly round-up dated 2 September 2010 ↗.
Wikiquote lists the line among its sourced quotes ↗ — not in its Disputed section — citing a Granada Television chat-show hosted by Shelley Rohde on Wednesday 20 May 1981.
Wikipedia reproduces the transcribed line from that interview ↗, cites the Granada recording of 20 May 1981, and states plainly that his most famous quotation is frequently paraphrased.
source.excerptNote: Per Wikipedia’s account of the interview ↗, Shankly had just said he put his “heart and soul” into football “to the extent that [his] family suffered”; Rohde asked whether he regretted that devotion, and “Yeah, I regret it very much” was his answer before he added the line. Wikiquote transcribes it slightly differently ↗: “Someone said to me ‘To you football is a matter of life or death!’ and I said ‘Listen, it’s more important than that’.”

author.name: Bill Shankly
author.heading: Bill Shankly
author.bio: Bill Shankly was a Scottish wing-half turned manager who took over a second-division Liverpool in 1959 and left it, fifteen years later, as one of the great institutions of English football. He managed Carlisle United, Grimsby Town, Workington and Huddersfield Town before Anfield, and his gift for the compressed, combative one-liner made him one of the most quoted figures the game has produced. He retired in 1974 and died in September 1981, four months after the television interview that produced his most famous sentence — and the paraphrase that displaced it.

misattribution.heading: What’s wrong with the famous version
misattribution.intro: Nobody else is claiming this line — it is Shankly’s, and the occasion is on film. What has drifted is the wording, and the story people tell about when he said it.

items.who: “Football is not a matter of life and death. It’s much more important than that”
items.why: Not a sentence Shankly is recorded as saying. In the interview he reports someone else’s remark and answers it: “Somebody said that football’s a matter of life and death to you. I said, ‘Listen, it’s more important than that.’” Wikipedia transcribes the line and notes the quotation is frequently paraphrased ↗. The tidied form circulates on aggregator sites, Goodreads among them ↗.

items.who: “Some people believe football is a matter of life and death, I am very disappointed with that attitude. I can assure you it is much, much more important than that”
items.why: A longer, more oratorical rewrite that the national press has printed as verbatim — it appears in the Daily Mirror’s Shankly round-up of 2 September 2010 ↗. The “I am very disappointed with that attitude” clause has no counterpart in the recorded exchange.

items.who: A press conference after a Merseyside derby, or a speech to the Kop in the 1960s
items.why: Versions of this setting circulate on quote and SEO pages, but I found no source documenting any of them. The documented occasion is the Granada Television interview broadcast on 20 May 1981, well after Shankly had left management, which is what Wikiquote cites in its sourced section ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: What he actually said, on camera: “Somebody said that football’s a matter of life and death to you. I said, ‘Listen, it’s more important than that.’” — Granada Television, broadcast 20 May 1981 ↗.

context.heading: The boast that was really a confession
lead: The famous version sounds like swagger — a hard man of the game telling you football outranks mortality. The moment it actually came from is much sadder. On 20 May 1981, sitting with Granada’s Shelley Rohde, Shankly said he had put his “heart and soul” into football “to the extent that [his] family suffered.” Rohde asked whether he regretted that. “Yeah, I regret it very much,” he said — and only then reached for the line.

He was seven years retired from Liverpool by then, and a little over four months from his death that September. The joke lands differently in context: a man ruefully repeating something someone else had once said about him, not a manager crowing in a press room.
detailsBody: The smoothed wording was entrenched long before the internet. Stephen F. Kelly’s 1997 biography, published by Virgin Books, is titled Bill Shankly: It’s Much More Important Than That — the paraphrase, not the transcript, had already become the shorthand for the man.

Notice what the recording shows about the grammar of the thing. Shankly never asserts that football is not a matter of life and death; he quotes somebody else’s characterisation of him and tops it. Every popular version turns that reported exchange into a flat declaration, which is exactly what makes it quotable — and exactly what makes it not his sentence.
context.pull: Yeah, I regret it very much.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikipedia states Shankly's most famous quotation is frequently paraphrased; that in a May 1981 interview with Granada Television presenter Shelley Rohde he said he put his "heart and soul" into football "to the extent that [his] family suffered"; that asked if he regretted it he replied "Yeah, I regret it very much" before adding "Somebody said that football's a matter of life and death to you. I said, 'Listen, it's more important than that.'"; and cites Granada Television, "Life And Death", 20 May 1981. It also gives his dates (2 September 1913 – 29 September 1981), Liverpool management 1959–1974, his earlier clubs, and lists Stephen F. Kelly, Bill Shankly: It's Much More Important Than That (Virgin Books, 1997) in its bibliography.

Wikiquote's Bill Shankly page lists, in its main sourced Quotes section and not in its Disputed section, "Someone said to me 'To you football is a matter of life or death!' and I said 'Listen, it's more important than that'.", cited to an interview on a Granada Television chat-show hosted by Shelley Rohde on Wednesday 20th of May 1981.

Goodreads hosts the exact circulating wording "Football is not a matter of life and death... it's much more important than that." attributed to Bill Shankly with no source, under the site's notice that quotes are added by the community and are not verified by Goodreads.

The archived Mirror Football blog post dated 02/09/10, headlined "Some people believe football is a matter of life and death... The wit and wisdom of Bill Shankly", prints as a Shankly quote: "Some people believe football is a matter of life and death, I am very disappointed with that attitude. I can assure you it is much, much more important than that."

The Guardian's 18 October 2009 profile "Bill Shankly: Life, death and football" quotes John Toshack — "His quote about football being more important than life or death, he really felt that way" — and Shankly's "At a football club, there's a holy trinity – the players, the manager and the supporters." Verified against the Wayback Machine capture of that article; the live Guardian URL was not directly fetchable.

A YouTube video at this URL is titled "Life And Death", matching the title, publisher and date Wikipedia cites for the Granada Television interview of 20 May 1981. Only the page title was confirmed by fetch; the video's contents were not independently transcribed here.
